what_happened: The job to tell the verifier that records/ and private paths are absent by design (a prompts-class change) failed. The producer stage did not finish: it hit its 1800-second deadline. No work product was delivered, and no acceptance criteria, findings or checks are listed. The failure came from the time limit, not from a verdict on the work.
cause: The producer runs against a fixed wall-clock deadline. Nothing in the job tracks progress, checks in partway, or tells a stalled producer from a slow one. A short prompt-edit job therefore burns the full 1800 seconds before anyone learns it is stuck. The event does not show why the producer ran long. Likely causes are a loop, a wait on something that never arrived, or a task wider than the request implied. The job keeps no partial state to diagnose this from or to resume from.
prevention: Add a producer progress watchdog. It would require a visible step, such as a file written or a commit made, within a short window (about 10 minutes). If none appears, it would stop the producer early and record its last activity and partial output as the failure reason. On a deadline hit, the system would save the partial workspace and offer one automatic retry from that point, with the failure reason passed to the new run. For prompt-class jobs, a lower deadline would make a stall show up sooner.
proposed_request: Add a progress watchdog to the producer stage. If the producer makes no observable progress (no file change or commit) for 10 minutes, stop it early. Record its last activity and keep the partial workspace. When a producer hits its deadline or is stopped by the watchdog, keep the partial work and retry once automatically, giving the retry the recorded failure reason. Then re-run job 20261010-154006-vc5k: update the verifier prompt to state that records/ and private paths are absent from the snapshot by design, so the verifier does not treat their absence as a defect. Acceptance: a test with a producer that stalls shows it stopped by the watchdog before the deadline, with its last activity recorded and its partial work kept.
